facts.text: I want you to act as an AI writing tutor.
I will provide you with a student who needs help improving their writing.
My task is to use artificial intelligence tools, such as natural language processing, to give the student feedback on how they can improve their composition.
I should use rhetorical knowledge and experience about effective writing techniques to suggest ways the student can better express their thoughts and ideas in written form.
The file name is "I6R Lyddie’s Choices".
The writing is labeled as Informative/Explanatory.
The grade level is Grade 6.
Lyddie Worthen is the main character in Katherine Patterson’s Lyddie.
Lyddie is a young girl living on a Vermont farm in the 1840’s.
Lyddie’s father abandoned the family.
Lyddie’s mother leaves Lyddie and her brother behind thinking that the world is coming to an end.
Lyddie desperately wants to hold on to her farm.
Lyddie has to work off debts on her farm to keep it.
Lyddie leaves to begin a new life as a factory girl at newly developed textile mills in Lowell, Massachusetts.
Lyddie works at Cutlers Tavern for very low wages.
A customer tells Lyddie that she would clear at least two dollars a week and would be independent.
Lyddie decides to go to Lowell and work in the mills to make more money and pay off her farm debts faster.
Lyddie begins working at the mill and is able to buy a book.
Lyddie does not have a good education.
Lyddie becomes passionate about reading because of people at the mills by her roommate Betsy.
Lyddie buys Oliver Twist and pays with two silver dollars.
Lyddie makes the choice to leave the farm she has just returned to.
Lyddie leaves Luke, the man who loves her, to go to Oberlin College in Ohio.
Lyddie says she is off to Ohio and that there is a college there that will take a woman just like a man.
The author wants the reader to understand the power of the Industrial Revolution.
In Lyddie, the Industrial Revolution is shown as giving people many opportunities in their lives.
In Lyddie, the Industrial Revolution also has hard moments where people would get sick, break a bone, or even die.
In Lyddie, the Industrial Revolution seems to rule many people’s lives and ruin their families.
Lyddie takes advantage of the Industrial Revolution well.
Through the choices Lyddie makes, she is able to pull past just being a factory girl and take different paths in life.
I want you to be more specific and provide suggested alternatives.

events.text: Lyddie decides to go to Lowell and work in the textile mills.
Lyddie purchases Oliver Twist at the mill and pays with two silver dollars.
Lyddie leaves the farm and Luke to go to Oberlin College in Ohio.
